title: Every spectral subset of the cyclic group of order p squared times q times r tiles, for distinct primes p, q and r
difficulty: After the precise prior cyclic spectral/tiling reductions, positive prime-coset decomposition, cube rule and Coven--Meyerowitz tiling criterion, the author still proves a modular projection lemma and combines it with a complete cardinality analysis. The coupled spectrum graphs and projected coset restrictions must simultaneously control the p-squared coordinate and both other prime directions to force a tiling. That residual structural classification is nonroutine rather than direct cyclotomic substitution, giving a conservative H1.

title: For every positive modulus, sufficiently high distinct-wise intersection divisibility bounds a set family by two to the floor of n divided by the modulus plus a constant, with no constant for large divisible n
difficulty: After ordinary finite-dimensional linear algebra and the named Boolean-points rank bound, the human proof still constructs disjoint-support coordinatewise products to isolate a low-dimensional exceptional coordinate set. Repeated doubling and prime-power lifts must then force large twin atoms of the prescribed modulus, followed by an exact matching-removal argument and atomic closing that improves a linear exceptional error to a constant. These coupled structural steps exceed routine qualification linear algebra or inclusion-exclusion, so the original primary result is conservatively H1.

title: Over every finite field other than F2, the slice, geometric and analytic ranks of a three-tensor satisfy SR at most three GR at most 8.13 AR
difficulty: After the exact classical tangent-dimension, determinantal-ideal and perfect-field stable-rank descent prerequisites, the author still constructs a common slice decomposition for an entire tangent matrix space and couples it to maximal-dimensional low-rank sections. A separate full argument turns degree/Bezout control and equidimensional envelopes into codimension-exponential finite-field zero-fibre bounds. Both remaining structural and uniform counting arguments are substantive beyond routine qualification substitutions, yielding conservative H1 for the combined original rank inequality.
